title: Finding the Sweet Spot: Preference Data Construction for Scaling Preference Optimization

summary.claim: When scaling on-policy samples, picking the highest-reward response as chosen and the lowest as rejected makes performance drop. Picking the rejected response at μ−2σ of the reward distribution keeps improving performance as samples grow.
summary.condition: DPO preference data built by repeated sampling and scored by a reward model; four models, evaluated on AlpacaEval 2.
summary.gap: (Inferred) Only general instruction-following is evaluated, so it is unknown whether this selection rule helps safety alignment or calibration.
